Consider the vector field $F=⟨y,\,0,\,2x⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of the solid onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?

Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,z,\,-y⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper paraboloid ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=z=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,R=-y.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-0\cdot (-2x)-(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot (-2y)+(-y))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(7y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨0,z,-y⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(7y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}8y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
